welcome_lead: Discover how the Sun, Moon and Earth line up to cast eclipses.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy: solar and lunar eclipses, geometry, umbra and penumbra.
final_note: Eclipses are alignments worth getting up early for.

concepts.def: Moon passes between Sun and Earth at a new moon.
Earth passes between Sun and Moon at a full moon.
Inner dark cone of shadow giving total eclipse.
Outer lighter shadow giving partial eclipse.
Sun (or Moon) is completely covered along umbra path.
Moon too small to cover Sun; ring of light remains.

walkthroughs.body_html: At new moon, the Moon can pass directly between Sun and Earth, casting its shadow on Earth. Observers in the umbra see a total eclipse; those in the penumbra see a partial eclipse.
At full moon, the Moon can enter Earth's shadow. The Moon often appears red because Earth's atmosphere bends red light into the umbra — a 'blood moon'.
The Moon's orbit is tilted ~5 degrees from the ecliptic. So most months the shadows miss. Only when alignments occur near the nodes do we see eclipses.
